Subject: Kickoff: MSA + Order Form for BlueHarbor Logistics — initial intake

Hi Grace,

Thanks for the quick intro — attaching our draft MSA and a populated order form so we can start. We have a few timeline constraints: the board wants executed paperwork by end of April and they asked procurement to prioritize Redwood because of the integration timeline.

Can you confirm:
- Who at Redwood will own redlines and where we should send changes (email vs Drive)?
- Typical turnaround for an initial redline from your legal team?
- Any standard security/compliance attachments you expect (SOC2 report, data processing addendum)?

Attached: BlueHarbor_MSA_v1.docx, OrderForm_BHL_2026.xlsx

High-level items for our counsel: data residency for EU customers, indemnity language, and a one-year service credit SLA carveout for scheduled maintenance. Our procurement counsel is cc'd on this thread (procurement@blueharborlogistics.com).

If easier, we're available for a 30-minute kickoff tomorrow morning PST.

Thanks,
Marta Ruiz
Director, Strategic Procurement
BlueHarbor Logistics

Quick response and next steps:

2) Laura (contracts) will lead legal redlines for the MSA. Please expect an initial pass within 48–72 hours for our comments; if BlueHarbor needs a faster turnaround, let us know and we'll prioritize.

Can you confirm the legal contact for the BlueHarbor counsel and which jurisdiction you'd like the agreement governed by? Also confirm the billing entity name and the PO number if you have one.

Marta / Grace — taking this on. Preliminary intake notes after a brief scan of the MSA you sent: 
- Data residency: the MSA references "Customer data may be stored in any region." We will propose a clause that BlueHarbor can require EU-only storage for EU customers (add an appendix). Please confirm expected customer distribution (approx %% EU vs US).
- Liability / Indemnity: we'll propose a liability cap tied to 12 months of fees or a fixed cap — need to know expected ARR for Year 1 so we can set an appropriate ceiling.
- SLA: Redwood's standard service credit language is in the template; we can review the one-year credit carveout you mentioned but will need concrete availability targets.

I'll upload our annotated MSA and a short comment summary to the Drive tracker. If BlueHarbor has in-house redlines, please send them as tracked changes in Word so we can merge.

Attachment: Redwood_MSA_template_comments.pdf (high-level notes)

I'll aim to circulate our first redline by end of day Friday PST. If you need the 48-hour turnaround, please confirm and we'll push to prioritize.

Laura Bennett
Senior Contracts Manager | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

- Governing law: Delaware is preferred for BlueHarbor (we can be flexible if Redwood has firm constraints).
- EU footprint: roughly 30% of our customers are EU-based; EU-only data residency will be material for us.
- Billing entity / PO: BlueHarbor Logistics, Inc. — PO # BHL-PO-3345 (attached vCard/PO ref).
- Procurement counsel: Ben Collins (Collins & More) — ben.collins@collinsandmore.com. He is copied on the separate procurement thread and available for comment.

We can do the Fri 09:00 PST kickoff if that helps to speed things. 48-hour turnaround would be ideal — procurement is on a tight calendar.

BlueHarbor Logistics

Looping back with operational suggestions before the kickoff: 
- I'll host a 30-min kickoff tomorrow 09:00 PST (Fri) — calendar invite to follow. Agenda: intake review, clarify data residency requirements, confirm SLA targets, and agree on a redline timeline.
- I've created a shared redline tracker in Drive for merging BlueHarbor's changes and our internal comments — link above. Please ask counsel to upload redlines as tracked changes in Word.
- Negotiation note for planning: if BlueHarbor seeks a liability cap higher than our standard, a common compromise is a multiple of annual fees (e.g., 3x fees) with a maximum cap ($1M) — suggest we table specifics until we have ARR estimate.

I'll also attach a short checklist for the kickoff (billing entity, PO, primary legal contact, required compliance docs such as SOC2). Attaching here for convenience.

Thanks — see you on the call.
